question:
A 27-year-old male presents to the office for evaluation of back pain for the past 2 years. The physical
exam is otherwise normal except for paraspinal tenderness to L1-L3. He has had a previous workup
with imaging that was negative for any alarming findings. Palpation reveals that he is restricted in right
sidebending and the transverse processes of L1-L3 are more anterior on the left. The decision is made

to use Still technique to address this patient’s somatic dysfunction. Before the patient is returned to
neutral at the end of the maneuver, in what position should the patient be? Answer Choices: (A) L2
neutral, sidebent left, rotated right (B) L2 flexed, sidebent right, rotated left (C) L2 extended, sidebent
right, rotated left (D) L2 neutral, sidebent right, rotated left (E) L2 neutral, sidebent right, rotated right
(F) L2 neutral, sidebent left, rotated left (G) L2 extended, sidebent left, rotated left (H) L2 extended,
sidebent right, rotated right (I) L2 flexed, sidebent right, rotated right (J) L2 flexed, sidebent left, rotated
right
 A. L2 extended, sidebent right, rotated left
B. L2 flexed, sidebent left, rotated right
C. L2 neutral, sidebent left, rotated right
D. L2 neutral, sidebent right, rotated right
E. L2 flexed, sidebent right, rotated left
F. L2 extended, sidebent left, rotated left
G. L2 neutral, sidebent right, rotated left
H. L2 extended, sidebent right, rotated right
I. L2 flexed, sidebent right, rotated right
J. L2 neutral, sidebent left, rotated left
